items.justification: Public disclosure policy versus internal threat modelling on configuration changes.
Both require secure erasure of data when it is no longer to be retained; A on user demand at the device, B on decommissioning of a model or system.
Update-integrity verification and general resilience to adversarial input are separate objectives that together harden the system against tampering.
Device update capability versus justifying the use of poorly documented components.
Both serve the delivery of security updates; A requires the device to support a secure update mechanism, B requires the supply chain to produce and deliver the updates.
Vulnerability monitoring and rectification versus usage guidance for end-users.
Publishing hardware replacement support versus cloud provider contractual flow-down.
Physical attack surface versus behavioural performance monitoring.
Software updateability versus documentation justifying component choice.
Tamper alerting on the device versus contractual arrangements with cloud operators.
A is a specific memory-protection control, B the threat analysis process that would motivate selecting it.
Timely remediation of disclosed vulnerabilities versus audit logging of prompt and configuration changes.
Mandating an authentication control and verifying that specified controls were actually implemented are distinct duties in the same assurance chain.
User control over update notifications versus asset tracking and version control.
Local operation through outages versus monitoring model behaviour over time.
Per-device password uniqueness versus supply-chain component justification.
Secure development practice and pre-deployment testing are different objectives that jointly govern a secure release.
Input validation prevents manipulation; logging records actions after the fact.
Secure storage of security parameters versus guidance on model limitations.
Credential change mechanism versus notifying end-users about security updates.
Physical interface exposure is a hardware design matter, whereas B addresses risks arising from new settings or configuration options.
A requires validation of unexpected network input; B requires withstanding unexpected inputs together with adversarial attacks and system failure, which contains A's obligation.
Both establish accountability for unauthorized change to a deployed system, A by alerting on detection and B by keeping an audit log of configuration changes.
Brute-force resistance versus continuous infrastructure risk review.
Both address continuity and recovery from disruption; A as device-level resilience, B as organizational disaster recovery planning.
Securing the update channel cryptographically and actually producing and delivering patches are distinct obligations that together make patching effective.
Physical attack surface versus incident support for end-users.
Both detect security-relevant change in a deployed system, A through integrity alerting and B through behavioural monitoring.
Both restrict access to system internals; A physically protects debug ports, B applies access-control measures to APIs, models and pipelines.
Password generation strength versus asset tracking and version control.
Both reduce exposure by separation and disabling what is not needed, A for unused interfaces and B for development environments under least privilege.
Both require operational data to be analysed for security anomalies; A covers device telemetry, B covers system logs and model behaviour including drift and poisoning.
Uniqueness of security parameters versus contingency planning where updates are impossible.
Prohibition on hard-coded credentials versus general resilience to adversarial AI attack.
User setup guidance versus independent security testing.
Isolability of non-updatable devices versus human oversight of AI systems.
Secure development process versus evaluating model outputs for unintended influence.
Limiting information disclosure at initialization versus threat modelling triggered by configuration change.
Minimising unauthenticated disclosure versus monitoring internal model states.
A mandates disclosure of sensing capabilities to the user; B mandates preventing disclosure of model internals. The obligations run in opposite directions.
